thread:
IncidentBot: ALERT: realtime-hosted-prod p99 latency > 3s for 5m (SLO breach). Alert group: latency-regression. Dash: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/latency/realtime-hosted-prod :rotating_light:
Marta (oncall): pinging oncall, I'm on it. paging phone -> ring, then DM 
Marta (oncall): @Ava can you join triage? looks cross-region but primarily us-west-2
Ava (SRE): oncall joining. grabbing p95/p99 timeseries. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.2s at 23:07 UTC. p99 spiked to 3.6s.
Jules (support): I'm seeing multiple customer tickets reporting streaming stalls in the last 10m — customers A, C, and D reporting drops and reconnects. forwarding sample logs.
Ravi (eng-runtime): seeing increased tail latencies on the streaming shard pool. KV cache hit rate dropped ~40% at the same time. suspicious.
Marta (oncall): incident severity? do we have active rollback or routing options?
Ava (SRE): initial triage checklist: 1) confirm signal (dash+traces) 2) identify blast radius 3) quick mitigation (routing/scale/rollback) 4) postmortem owner.
Ava (SRE): Confirmed signal: cpu/gpu utilization normal, queue depth increased on streaming workers, worker latencies show long GC-ish pauses on 3 pods. logs show repeated `msg=stalling write to client` from streamer.
Ravi (eng-runtime): paste logs:
```
2026-03-14T23:07:12Z streamer[shard-7]: stall detected: backpressure=high, kv_cache_miss=0.62, write_wait=1264ms
2026-03-14T23:07:15Z serve[shard-3]: grpc_send timeout 1200ms
```
Marta (oncall): hitting the runbooks: check model fallbacks and routing. ops-bot, can we open a mitigation route and scale streaming-pool?
ops-bot: Mitigation runbook step executed: increased streaming-pool replicas from 4 -> 8 (provisioning). Created rollback ticket #INC-17910.
Jules (support): letting affected customers know we're actively investigating and performing mitigation. posting status -> status.redwood.com update draft.
Liam (product): any customer-facing SLA impact? p99 > SLO now so likely. mark as SLA impact yes.
Ava (SRE): quick experiment: traffic split to fallback model variant (less latency-optimized quantized model) for 15% of sessions. Command:
```
redwood route modify --service realtime-hosted-prod --split fallback=15
```
Ravi (eng-runtime): Split applied. Also disabling aggressive batching on streaming pool (set batch_threshold=1) to reduce head-of-line blocking.
Marta (oncall): handoff: I'm primary until stabilization. Ava and Ravi on escalation. Jules handling comms.
Ava (SRE): after scale + routing, p95 dropped from 1200ms -> 420ms within 90s. p99 dropped below 2.1s but still above target. Streaming stall errors decreased by ~70%.
Jules (support): customers A & C acknowledged improved behavior. customer D still seeing reconnects (session id 0x9f4). collecting more logs.
Ravi (eng-runtime): observed correlated spike in KV cache eviction rate around the time of regression — new model rollout earlier today might have changed tokenization leading to cache churn. checking rollout history...
ops-bot: Deployment history: model-realtime-v3 deployed 02:30 UTC today to canary (10%) then ramped to 100% at 16:45 UTC.
Ava (SRE): interesting — ramp to 100% happened earlier, but parameter change in v3 quant layer could affect cache keying. can we roll v3 -> v2 for streaming routes as an experiment?
Marta (oncall): Do we have a safe rollback window?
Ravi (eng-runtime): We can route streaming to v2 for now: `redwood route modify --service realtime-hosted-prod --model v2=100 --mode streaming` — executing in 30s.
Ava (SRE): executing rollback for streaming-only traffic.
ops-bot: Route update applied: streaming traffic -> model v2 (100%).
Marta (oncall): watch metrics.
Ava (SRE): within 60s after routing to v2, p99 holds at ~650ms, p95 ~220ms. Streaming stalls drop to baseline.
Jules (support): posting update to customers: mitigation in place, continued monitoring.
Liam (product): open incident page + postmortem owner? I can own postmortem and coordinate with runtime team.
Marta (oncall): creating incident record INC-17910 and linking dashboards/traces. followups: 1) root cause: confirm v3 cache key behavior 2) test harness for quantized tokenization changes 3) better canary health checks for tail latency 4) alert tune to correlate kv_cache_miss spikes.
Ravi (eng-runtime): action items assigned: I'll revert rollout for streaming and create a reproducible test. @Ava please capture SRE mitigation timeline.
Ava (SRE): capturing timeline and adding traces + flamegraphs. Will add RCA draft.
Marta (oncall): closing the active page now. we'll keep thread open for 1hr for watch. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
IncidentBot: Incident INC-17910 created. Severity: Sev2. Pager cleared from on-call.
Jules (support): final customer note prepared. posting in 5m.
Marta (oncall): postmortem owner: Liam. ETA draft in 48h.
Ravi (eng-runtime): follow-up notes: add synthetic streaming tail test in CI that measures p99 under burst load.
Ava (SRE): adding alert rule to fire when kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.25 AND p99 > 1s across 5m.
Marta (oncall): thanks team. keeping channel for updates.
